questions.prompt: Where was the lowest air temperature ever recorded on Earth (WMO)?
questions.teaser: Where was the coldest temperature ever recorded?
questions.turnsOut: Vostok Station, high on the East Antarctic ice sheet: −89.2 °C (−128.6 °F) on 21 July 1983. Satellites have since found snow surfaces nearby at around −98 °C, but that is the ground, not the air the record is about.
questions.sourceTitle: WMO Weather and Climate Extremes Archive: records table (31 July 2025)

questions.prompt: Where did the most rain ever recorded fall in 24 hours (WMO)?
questions.teaser: Where did the most rain ever fall in one day?
questions.turnsOut: Foc-Foc, 2,290 m up on the volcanic island of La Réunion: 1,825 mm in 24 hours on 7–8 January 1966, as Tropical Cyclone Denise passed. The same storm set the 12-hour record too: 1,144 mm.
questions.sourceTitle: WMO Weather and Climate Extremes Archive: records table (31 July 2025)

questions.prompt: Where was the strongest wind gust ever measured, outside a tornado (WMO)?
questions.teaser: Where was the strongest gust of wind ever measured?
questions.turnsOut: Barrow Island, off Western Australia: 113.2 m/s (408 km/h) as Cyclone Olivia passed on 10 April 1996. The WMO only confirmed it in 2010, ending the reign of Mount Washington's 103.3 m/s gust from 1934.
questions.sourceTitle: WMO Weather and Climate Extremes Archive: records table (31 July 2025)
